title: Analytical Uncertainty-Based Loss Weighting in Multi-Task Learning (UW-SO; GCPR 2024)
text: checked (abstract + html v1): the closed form of Kendall's uncertainty weighting is sigma_k = L_k (L1 case), i.e. weight 1/L_k; UW-SO uses it with a stop-gradient on the batch losses and a softmax of temperature T, w_k = softmax(1/(L_k T)), total = sum w_k L_k: zero extra passes, one hyperparameter (T found after a quarter of the training). Delta_m % (lower better) NYUv2 ResNet-50: equal weights -7.1, UW -7.2, UW-SO -9.8, grid-searched fixed weights -9.7, IMTL-L -7.7; Cityscapes 5.3 / 0.5 / 0.3 / 2.1; CelebA (40 tasks) -2.4 / -0.1 / -4.0. A bounded, free replacement of our Kendall term. Blockers: 2-3 task dense benchmarks only, no BEV, no code found, T ranges 2-100 across benchmarks and must be searched on our loss scale, weights follow 1/L so a high-floor group (thin lines) gets less weight. Use as the first arm against the fixed-weight control.
idea: closed-form 1/L weights with softmax temperature; floor on the weights

title: FAMO: Fast Adaptive Multitask Optimization (NeurIPS 2023)
text: checked (abstract + ar5iv + repo): softmax task weights z updated from the change of the log losses (one gradient step on the MGDA objective min_z |J z|^2 with J the gradients of log l_i), model step on one scalar so O(1) space and time in the number of tasks; the official trainer adds one no-grad forward pass per step to get the new losses (the paper text does not say so). NYUv2 Delta_m % lower better: equal weights 5.59, PCGrad 3.97, CAGrad 0.20, Nash-MTL -4.04, FAMO -4.10; CityScapes FAMO 8.13 vs Nash-MTL 6.82 (table garbled). Core class about 35 lines, gamma 0.001-0.01 on the logits, Adam lr 0.025. Blockers: extra forward pass (about +30 % step time, estimate), gamma sensitive, losses must be positive (shift by a lower bound), no BEV result, later O(1) methods score better on NYUv2 (GO4Align -6.08 per a 2025 table). Use as the second arm if UW-SO fails.
idea: log-loss-rate weights; extra no-grad forward for the update

title: In Defense of the Unitary Scalarization for Deep Multi-Task Learning (NeurIPS 2022)
text: checked (abstract + ar5iv text): plain summed losses plus ordinary single-task regularisation (dropout in the heads 0.25-0.5, weight decay 1e-3 on CelebA and 1e-5 on Cityscapes, early stopping on validation) match or beat MGDA, IMTL, PCGrad, GradDrop and RLW on Multi-MNIST, CelebA (40 tasks), Cityscapes and Meta-World MT10 / MT50 (numbers only in figures; Nash-MTL and CAGrad not compared). Overheads: PCGrad about 35x slower than scalarisation on CelebA, IMTL / MGDA / GradDrop 1.6-2.3x on Cityscapes, memory a factor m (tasks) lower. Our fixed weighting with count-normalised terms is this control. Blockers: figure-only results, 2 dense tasks, 2022 optimisers. Use as the protocol of the control arm.
idea: control = summed normalised losses + tuned regularisation

title: Do Current Multi-Task Optimization Methods in Deep Learning Even Help? (NeurIPS 2022)
text: checked (ar5iv text): MGDA, GradNorm, PCGrad, IMTL and RLW land on the Pareto front of scalarisation weights and not beyond it on Transformer NMT (about 120M parameters) and Cityscapes (segmentation + depth, ResNet-50); CelebA average error scalarisation 9.23 test vs MGDA 9.53 and PCGrad 9.35, while published scalarisation baselines range from 8.71 to 9.99 (under-tuned baselines); a sparse learning-rate grid moves results 6-7x more than the seed spread; scale of the model shifts the front more than the method. Protocol for any balancing arm: tune lr per arm, compare along several weight vectors, judge the whole trade-off. Blockers: NMT-dominated, grid search of weights is expensive, no CAGrad / Nash-MTL / FAMO. Use as the evaluation protocol.
idea: compare on the Pareto front over weight vectors; per-arm lr grid

title: FULLER: Unified Multi-modality Multi-task 3D Perception via Multi-level Gradient Calibration
text: checked (abstract + ar5iv): on a BEVFusion-style camera + LiDAR model, IMTL-G computed at the LAST shared layer balances detection and map segmentation, and a momentum-smoothed gate on the per-modality gradient norms scales each sensor branch. nuScenes val: 1:1 multi-task baseline mAP 59.1 / NDS 65.0 / map mIoU 44.0 -> 60.5 / 65.3 / 58.4; single-task segmentation reference 62.3; three-task variant loses 1.3 mAP. The only gradient-balancing result on a multi-task BEV model found. Blockers: the 1:1 baseline looks badly weighted (no hand-tuned weight tried, cf. BEVerse [1, 10, 1]), no PCGrad or uncertainty baseline in the text read, camera + LiDAR, no code. Watch: take the feature-level gradient trick, not the numbers.
idea: gradients at the shared BEV feature; IMTL-G 4x4 Gram; per-sensor gradient gate

title: Jacobian Descent for Multi-Objective Optimization (UPGrad; TorchJD)
text: checked (abstract + html v3 first part + repo + docs): the update is an aggregator of the Jacobian (one row per objective); UPGrad projects each gradient onto the dual cone of all gradients and averages (plain mean when none conflict), solved as a QP over m variables on the Gramian. Paper experiments are instance-wise risk minimisation on 1,024-image subsets of six small datasets only; NYUv2 / Cityscapes / CelebA are not used and the authors ask for better multi-task benchmarks. Library TorchJD (MIT, PyTorch 2.3+) has 23 aggregators (UPGrad, CAGrad, IMTL-G, Nash-MTL, PCGrad, Aligned-MTL, GradDrop ...) and 12 scalarizers (FAMO, IMTL-L, UW, DWA, STCH ...) behind mtl_backward / jac_to_grad. Blockers: the Jacobian is over the shared parameters (about K trunk backward passes, inference), autogram engine needs batch-independent modules (BatchNorm is the counterexample), no multi-task benchmark. Watch as the ablation harness if groups conflict.
idea: one library for scalarizers and aggregators; mtl_backward on four heads

title: Conflict-Averse Gradient Descent for Multi-task Learning (CAGrad; NeurIPS 2021)
text: checked (html v2 + repo): maximise the worst-case task improvement inside a ball of radius c|g0| around the mean gradient, solved in a K-dimensional dual; c = 0 is plain gradient descent, large c is MGDA; needs K backward passes (CAGrad-Fast subsamples tasks). NYUv2 Delta_m % lower better: MTAN equal weights 5.59, MGDA 1.38, PCGrad 3.97, GradDrop 3.58, CAGrad 0.20; Cityscapes 22.60 / 18.29 / 11.64 (CAGrad). Later tables put Nash-MTL and FAMO at -4.1 on the same NYUv2 rows. Blockers: K gradients at the parameters, c tuned per benchmark (0.2 or 0.4, the paper contradicts itself), weak equal-weight baseline, no BEV. The MIT repo says FAMO is the successor. Watch as the reference of the gradient-based family.
idea: worst-case improvement in a ball around the mean gradient; K-dim dual

title: Auto-Lambda: Disentangling Dynamic Task Relationships (TMLR 2022)
text: checked (abstract + text mirror + repo + LICENSE): bilevel task weights lambda updated by the validation loss of the primary tasks through a finite-difference step; extra cost two forward and two backward passes per approximation step, about 3x the training time of equal weighting on CelebA. Delta MTL (here higher is better) NYUv2: equal +3.57, uncertainty +6.50, Auto-Lambda +8.21; Cityscapes +0.92 / +0.86 / +2.56. Blockers: custom Imperial College licence (non-commercial / academic research only), 3x cost, needs a validation signal, 3 dense tasks at most. Context only.
licence: custom Imperial College licence: non-commercial research only

title: Dual-Balancing for Multi-Task Learning (DB-MTL)
text: checked (abstract + html v3): loss-scale balancing by training on sum log(l_t + 1e-8) (Proposition 3.1: this is IMTL-L, the form of Kendall weighting), plus gradient balancing: each task gradient at the shared parameters gets an EMA, unit length, then the largest norm as common scale. Delta_p (higher better, vs single-task): NYUv2 equal weights -1.78, PCGrad -1.57, CAGrad -0.27, Nash-MTL -1.01, DB-MTL +1.15; Cityscapes -2.05 / -2.36 / -0.87 / -1.11 / +0.20; QM9 (11 tasks) DB-MTL best multi-task method at -58.10 but still below single-task. Blockers: the gradient half needs K gradients, metric differs from Delta_m, no authors' repo on the pages (LibMTL, MIT, has DB_MTL, FAMO, UW, IMTL, UPGrad, 26 methods). Watch: take the log transform as the scale-invariance argument.
idea: log-loss for scale invariance (equals Kendall optimum); max-norm gradient normalisation

title: Towards Impartial Multi-task Learning (IMTL-L and IMTL-G; ICLR 2021)
text: checked on a text mirror: IMTL-L = sum (e^{s_t} L_t - s_t), i.e. Kendall's form with the sign of s flipped; IMTL-G = closed-form task weights giving the aggregated gradient equal projection on every task gradient, computed w.r.t. the shared FEATURE so the backbone is backpropagated once. Seconds per iteration on Cityscapes: uniform 1.201, uncertainty / IMTL-L about 1.20, GradNorm 1.742, PCGrad 2.087, IMTL-G feature level 1.776, parameter level 2.769. NYUv2 mIoU: single-task 56.82, uncertainty 57.20, IMTL-L 58.36, hybrid 58.85. No arXiv id found (id here is a placeholder), no code released on the text read (LibMTL and TorchJD implement it). Blockers: 2-3 tasks, 2021 baselines. Context: the cost table and the feature-level trick.
idea: gradient balance at the shared feature; IMTL-L equals our Kendall term

title: Radar-Camera BEV Multi-Task Learning with Cross-Task Attention Bridge for Joint 3D Detection and Segmentation
text: checked (arXiv html v2, 2026-05-26): camera (ResNet-50 BEVDepth-style) + radar (RadarBEVNet) fused to a shared 256x128x128 BEV (0.8 m cells), CenterHead detection plus a 0.5 m segmentation decoder; losses balanced by Kendall uncertainty weighting with log sigma clamped at 1.5, segmentation loss = focal (alpha 0.25 gamma 3) + Dice, each x20. nuScenes val: joint baseline NDS 55.7 / mAP 44.4 / mIoU-7 42.9 against single-task RCBEVDet NDS 56.8 / mAP 45.3; the bridge (+0.58M parameters) leaves detection unchanged and adds +0.6 mIoU-7. GradNorm and PCGrad are only named in related work, no ablation of the balancing. Closest published setting to ours (camera + radar BEV, Kendall + clamp). Blockers: one A6000, no code link on the page, no thin-line task. Context.
idea: Kendall with a clamp on log sigma in a camera + radar BEV model

title: MATS: A novel multi-modality multi-task learning framework for 3D perception in autonomous driving
text: checked (arXiv html v1, 2026-07-27): negative transfer between detection and map segmentation is attacked by architecture (three fusion branches giving several BEV maps, task-specific mixture-of-experts with own gates), not by loss balancing: fixed weights 1.0 detection / 2.0 segmentation taken from the baselines, no GradNorm / PCGrad / uncertainty comparison. UniTR on nuScenes val: single-task 66.7 mAP / 70.3 NDS / 63.2 mIoU; naive multi-task 66.1 / 70.1 / 59.8; with MATS 67.5 / 70.8 / 64.6; parameters 39.3M -> 44.5M. Evidence that the cost of joint training falls on the map head (-3.4 mIoU). Blockers: camera + LiDAR, no latency, no code on the page. Context.
idea: separate BEV maps per task instead of gradient surgery

title: LDC-MTL: Balancing Multi-Task Learning through Scalable Loss Discrepancy Control
text: checked (abstract + html v3): bilevel loss-discrepancy control, weights from a softmax router on shared features, single-loop first-order algorithm, O(1) time and memory in the number of tasks, at most 1.11x the time of linear scalarisation (Nash-MTL about 12x on CelebA). NYU-v2 Delta_m % (lower better) LDC-MTL -4.40 +- 0.74 vs LS 5.59, FAMO -4.10, Nash-MTL -4.04, FairGrad -4.66, GO4Align -6.08 as printed (two of them better); Cityscapes -0.57 +- 1.17. Normalisation per dataset (QM9 log(l / l_0), NYU-v2 none). Blockers: no code link on the page, per-dataset step size and lambda, 2-3 dense tasks. Watch as the 2025 O(1) competitor of FAMO.
idea: router weights with loss-discrepancy penalty; log(l / l_0) normalisation

title: GO4Align: Group Optimization for Multi-Task Alignment
text: checked (abstract only): adaptive group-based risk minimisation, tasks are grouped by their interactions and risk information of earlier iterations guides the grouping; claims better results at lower compute than gradient methods. NYUv2 Delta_m -6.08 only as printed in the LDC-MTL table (digest, paper body not read). Blockers: grouping three or four tasks is trivial for us, no code link on the page. Context.

title: Independent Component Alignment for Multi-Task Learning (Aligned-MTL; CVPR 2023)
text: checked (abstract only): the condition number of the task-gradient system is the stability measure; Aligned-MTL aligns the orthogonal components of the gradients so that the update converges to the optimum of PRE-SET task weights (unlike most gradient methods); segmentation, instance segmentation, depth, normals and RL. Code https://github.com/SamsungLabs/MTL named on the page (licence not read; the paper is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); available as an aggregator in TorchJD and a method in LibMTL. Needs K gradients. Context.
idea: gradient alignment that keeps the chosen task weights

title: Smooth Tchebycheff Scalarization for Multi-Objective Optimization (STCH; ICML 2024)
text: digest (search summary, abstract not fetched): a smooth, differentiable version of the min-max Tchebycheff scalarisation that reaches all Pareto solutions under mild conditions with much faster convergence than the classic form; code https://github.com/Xi-L/STCH (from the summary). Also a scalarizer in TorchJD and a method in LibMTL (both checked). Targets the worst task, which matches the rule that no group may starve. Blockers: not read, licence not read, no dense or BEV result known. Context.

title: Planning-oriented Autonomous Driving (UniAD)
text: checked (arXiv html, first 100k of 130k characters): tracking, mapping, motion, occupancy and planning modules trained in two stages, perception (tracking + mapping) for 6 epochs, then end-to-end for 20 epochs, which the authors call empirically more stable; per-module loss weights are in the supplement (not read), no balancing algorithm. Table 2: naive multi-task baseline with separate heads against the full model: minADE -15.2 %, minFDE -17.0 %, occupancy IoU-far +4.9, average planning L2 -0.15. Context for the warm-up of plan 8.4 (dt = 0 first).
idea: staged training instead of loss balancing
